title: China just closed a gap in chipmaking that nobody talks about. The wafer size tells you how far it has to go.
excerpt: Hwatsing built China's first metrology system integrated with wafer polishing equipment. The six-inch format places it well short of advanced logic.
content_html:
Hwatsing Technology, China’s leading producer of chemical mechanical polishing equipment, announced a metrology system for six-inch wafers on Thursday that can be built directly into the polishing workflow. The company describes it as China’s first six-inch metrology system paired with CMP equipment.

The integration is the substantive part. Rather than measuring wafers separately after processing, the system takes readings before and after polishing and feeds live data back to the control system, according to the South China Morning Post.

Why polishing matters more than it sounds

Chemical mechanical polishing flattens and smooths the silicon disc between processing layers. Modern chips stack dozens of layers, and each one has to be planar to within nanometres or the next layer prints badly.

It is unglamorous work that determines yield. Closing the measurement loop should improve wafer uniformity and cut waste, which matters more in a country whose fabs run older lithography and need every point of yield they can find.

The number in the announcement

Six inches is 150mm. Leading-edge logic runs on 300mm wafers, and the sub-10nm nodes that export controls exist to restrict are made nowhere else.

The 150mm format belongs to mature nodes and compound semiconductors, and even there it is being left behind. Silicon carbide power devices are already migrating from 150mm to 200mm in volume manufacturing, while gallium nitride is moving from 200mm towards 300mm.

None of that makes the tool unimportant. It does mean this is a step on a ladder rather than a jump to the top of it.

What Hwatsing has actually achieved

The company’s track record is the stronger signal. China’s share of the global CMP equipment market rose from roughly 1.5% in 2022 to almost 11% in 2023, with Hwatsing responsible for most of the gain, according to Georgetown’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology.

Volume backs that up. Hwatsing shipped its 1,000th CMP system in April and has said it is targeting advanced chip manufacturing next.

It is spending accordingly, seeking up to 4 billion yuan, around $552 million, through a private placement to expand capacity, build out wafer reclamation services, and fund high-end tool development. A separate $237 million plant investment is also underway.

Applied Materials still leads the CMP market decisively, with Ebara holding roughly 27% globally. Eleven percent is a real position, not a dominant one.

The lithography problem it does not solve

Polishing tools are not the binding constraint. ASML remains the only company making EUV lithography machines, and China cannot buy them at any price under US-led export controls.

That is where the more consequential work is happening. China’s homegrown immersion DUV tool now has a name, Shanghai Aishengna, and a domestic DUV machine would matter considerably more than a metrology upgrade, though independent analysts have attached heavy caveats to reported progress there.

The strategy underneath

Beijing’s approach is to close every gap it can while the hardest one stays shut. Chinese semiconductor equipment self-sufficiency has reportedly reached around 35%, up from roughly 25% two years earlier.

Washington is weighing further restrictions on chip equipment sales, with Beijing arguing that cutting the supply chain damages everyone in it. Each round of controls has accelerated the localisation it was meant to prevent.

What success looks like when it arrives

China has already proved it can build a world-scale chip company in a segment where the tools are obtainable. Memory maker CXMT jumped 466% on its Shanghai debut to become the most valuable listed DRAM company in the country.

Demand is following. Apple has begun testing CXMT memory chips, which is roughly the highest-profile validation a Chinese chipmaker can receive.

CXMT still depends on foreign equipment it cannot always get. That is precisely the dependency tools like Hwatsing’s are meant to unwind, one process step at a time, which is slower than a breakthrough but harder to sanction.

content_html_zh:
中国领先的化学机械抛光设备生产商华清科技周四宣布推出一款适用于六英寸晶圆的计量系统，该系统可以直接构建到抛光工作流程中。 该公司将其描述为中国首个与 CMP 设备搭配的六英寸计量系统。

整合是实质性的部分。 据《南华早报》报道，该系统不是在加工后单独测量晶圆，而是在抛光前后读取读数，并将实时数据反馈给控制系统。

为什么抛光比听起来更重要

化学机械抛光使处理层之间的硅盘变平和光滑。 现代芯片堆叠了数十层，每一层的平面度都必须在纳米以内，否则下一层的打印效果会很差。

决定产量的是乏味的工作。 关闭测量环路应该可以提高晶圆的均匀性并减少浪费，这对于一个晶圆厂运行较旧的光刻技术并需要他们能找到的每一点良率的国家来说更为重要。

公告中的号码

六英寸是150毫米。 领先的逻辑在 300 毫米晶圆上运行，而受出口管制限制的 10 纳米以下节点则无处可寻。

150mm格式属于成熟节点和化合物半导体，但即便如此，它也被抛在了后面。 碳化硅功率器件的批量生产已经从 150mm 转向 200mm，而氮化镓则从 200mm 转向 300mm。

所有这些都并不意味着该工具不重要。 这确实意味着这是梯子上的一步，而不是跳到梯子的顶部。

华清实际取得了什么成就

该公司的往绩记录是更强烈的信号。 根据乔治城安全与新兴技术中心的数据，中国在全球 CMP 设备市场的份额从 2022 年的约 1.5% 上升到 2023 年的近 11%，其中 Hwatsing 贡献了大部分增长。

成交量证明了这一点。 Hwatsing 于 4 月份交付了第 1,000 套 CMP 系统，并表示下一步的目标是先进芯片制造。

该公司正在相应地进行支出，通过私募寻求高达 40 亿元人民币（约合 5.52 亿美元）的资金，以扩大产能、建立晶圆回收服务并为高端工具开发提供资金。 另一项 2.37 亿美元的工厂投资也正在进行中。

应用材料公司仍然在 CMP 市场占据决定性的领先地位，荏原在全球占有大约 27% 的份额。 百分之十一是一个真实的位置，而不是一个主导位置。

它没有解决的光刻问题

抛光工具不是约束条件。 ASML仍然是唯一一家生产EUV光刻机的公司，在美国主导的出口管制下，中国无法以任何价格购买它们。

这就是更重要的工作正在进行的地方。 中国自主研发的浸入式 DUV 工具现在有了一个名字：上海艾圣纳，国产 DUV 机器比计量升级更重要，尽管独立分析师对报告的进展提出了严格的警告。

下面的策略

北京的做法是尽可能缩小每一个差距，同时缩小最困难的差距。 据报道，中国半导体设备自给率已达到 35% 左右，而两年前约为 25%。

华盛顿正在考虑进一步限制芯片设备的销售，而北京则认为切断供应链会损害供应链中的每个人。 每一轮的控制都加速了其本应阻止的本地化。

成功到来时是什么样子

中国已经证明，它可以在可以获得工具的领域建立世界级芯片公司。 内存制造商长鑫存储在上海上市后股价上涨 466%，成为国内市值最高的 DRAM 上市公司。

需求如下。 苹果已经开始测试 CXMT 内存芯片，这大概是中国芯片制造商能收到的最引人注目的验证。

长鑫存储仍然依赖国外设备，但并不总能获得。 这正是 Hwatsing 之类的依赖工具的目的，一次一个流程步骤，这比突破要慢，但更难批准。
